central_moments — 3D moment_invariant op

• Data kinds: points → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.central_moments(points, max_order: 'int' = 3) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import moments3d; moments3d.central_moments(points, max_order: 'int' = 3) -> 'dict'; from the registry, ops3d.get("central_moments"))

Usage

The centroid-centred central moments μ_{pqr} (translation invariant; keys are (p,q,r)).

μ_{pqr} = mean( (x-x̄)^p (y-ȳ)^q (z-z̄)^r ). Includes all orders with p+q+r <= max_order. Computed after subtracting the centroid, so it is exactly translation invariant. Under the equal-mass convention μ_{000}=1, and the 1st-order moments μ_{100}=μ_{010}=μ_{001}=0 (a consequence of centring).

Parameters

points : array_like, shape (N, 3)

Point cloud.

max_order : int

Maximum order p+q+r to include (default 3). 0 or greater.

Returns

dict[tuple[int, int, int], float]

(p, q, r) → μ_{pqr}.

Notes:

• The number of keys in the returned dict is all combinations with p+q+r <= max_order (20 for max_order=3). Values are float (a mean, so divided by the number of points).

• Units are length^(p+q+r). Translation invariant but not invariant to rotation or scale (for rotation invariants see moment_invariants / principal_moments).

• 2nd-order moments such as (2,0,0), (1,1,0) are exactly the population covariance (divided by N), the same material as inertia_tensor.

• Higher orders are dominated by points far from the centroid, so they are sensitive to outliers. Consider statistical_outlier_removal or similar beforehand.

• Input is (N,3), N >= 1. max_order < 0, invalid shape or non-finite values raise ValueError. Deterministic.
